acceptance_criteria: AC-1 A record whose external_participant is true, whose relay is open and whose phase is not terminal classifies as handed_over.
AC-2 The same record without the flag classifies exactly as it does today, exited_without_close, and a test asserts it.
AC-3 A terminal phase, and a closed relay, each still win over the flag.
AC-4 derive_health returns a member of ALL_HEALTH_VALUES for every input in the existing generated matrix, which now has seven members.
AC-5 A handed_over movement is never classified silent on idle time alone.
AC-6 tests/test_orchestrator_dashboard.py passes with the new tests, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/GOV_ORCH_4B_A_PARTICIPANT_THE_ORCHESTRATOR_DID_NOT_SPAWN.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner approved 2026-09-15: HB-1 adds the seventh value handed_over to the closed set; HB-2 selects it only from the state record's own external_participant field and never infers it from a missing pid, so a spawned movement whose process died still reports exited_without_close, default-closed; HB-3 leaves precedence otherwise unchanged, a terminal outcome still wins and awaiting_po still comes next; HB-4 stops treating idle time as a stuck signal for such a movement.
baseline.engineering_baseline: scripts/orchestrator_dashboard.py owns derive_health and the closed value set. Two movements have already run on the hybrid path, NXS-LOCAL-0183 and NXS-LOCAL-0184, and both were shown as exited while succeeding.
baseline.product_baseline: Not a product change. The Java product, its collectors and its UI are untouched.
baseline.test_baseline: tests/test_orchestrator_dashboard.py passes on origin/main today, run locally on 2026-09-15 before this packet was written.
baseline.what_exists:
scripts/orchestrator_dashboard.py, around line 105, declares the closed set exactly like this:

HEALTH_HEALTHY = "healthy"
HEALTH_SILENT = "silent"
HEALTH_EXITED_WITHOUT_CLOSE = "exited_without_close"
HEALTH_AWAITING_PO = "awaiting_po"
HEALTH_FAILED = "failed"
HEALTH_DONE = "done"
ALL_HEALTH_VALUES = frozenset({
    HEALTH_HEALTHY, HEALTH_SILENT, HEALTH_EXITED_WITHOUT_CLOSE,
    HEALTH_AWAITING_PO, HEALTH_FAILED, HEALTH_DONE,
})

and the classifier itself, around line 265, ends exactly like this:

    if relay_status == "CLOSED" or phase in (orch.PHASE_DONE, orch.PHASE_CANCELLED):
        return HEALTH_DONE
    if phase == orch.PHASE_FAILED:
        return HEALTH_FAILED
    if next_actor == "po":
        return HEALTH_AWAITING_PO
    if not pid_alive:
        return HEALTH_EXITED_WITHOUT_CLOSE
    if idle_seconds is not None and idle_seconds >= stuck_after_seconds:
        return HEALTH_SILENT
    return HEALTH_HEALTHY

A real state record written by the hybrid path carries these keys and values, among others: "provider": "antigravity", "pid": null, "phase": "running", "merge_mode": "orchestrator", "last_action": "handed_over", "external_participant": true. A record written by a dispatch carries no external_participant key at all.

invariants: The value set stays closed and derive_health still returns exactly one member of it.
Default-closed: the new value is reachable only through the explicit field.
A spawned movement's classification is byte-for-byte what it is today.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Stop the workbench reporting a failure for a movement that was never a process. A movement handed to a participant the orchestrator cannot spawn has no pid by design, so derive_health falls through to exited_without_close and shows a successful movement as exited. GOV.ORCH.4-B adds a seventh value, handed_over, selected only from the record's own explicit flag.
output_contract: A workbench that shows work in progress as work in progress, and a failure only when there is one.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One pure function, one constant, and its tests, against a frozen clause that states the rule and its precedence exactly.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Both commands run from the repository root.
Every changed function names the clause it implements (GOV.ORCH.4-B HB-n).
Run only the commands named above.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE names where in the precedence chain you placed the rule and what proves a record without the flag is unchanged.
risks: Inferring the new state from a null pid, which would relabel a genuinely crashed dispatch as healthy work in progress -- the exact failure HB-2 forbids.
Placing the new rule before the terminal or awaiting_po rules, which would hide a finished or blocked movement.
Changing a caller's default so that a record without the flag behaves differently from today.

in: scripts/orchestrator_dashboard.py: add HEALTH_HANDED_OVER = "handed_over" to the constants and to ALL_HEALTH_VALUES.

derive_health: accept the record's external_participant as an explicit argument and return handed_over for it, positioned exactly where HB-3 puts it -- after the terminal and awaiting_po rules, in place of the dead-process rule and only for a record carrying the flag. A record without the flag must reach the existing rules unchanged.
Update every caller in this file so the flag reaches derive_health from the record; a caller that has no record field passes the default, which must behave exactly as today.

tests/test_orchestrator_dashboard.py: the four cases GOV.ORCH.4-B section 4 names -- the flag returns handed_over; no flag still returns exited_without_close; a terminal phase or a closed relay still wins over the flag; and whatever the input, the return value is still one member of the closed set, now of seven.
out: Any change to the six existing values, their spellings, or their meanings.
Any change to the stuck detector for a spawned movement, or to the usage and cost fields of GOV.ORCH.4 sections 3.1 and 3.2.
Inferring the new value from a missing pid, an absent log, a provider name, or anything other than the explicit field. HB-2 is default-closed and this is the clause the movement exists to honour.
Any change to scripts/orchestrator.py, to the state record writer, or to any document under docs/design/.
HB-4's lane-commit display. Not showing an idle time is enough here; rendering the lane's last commit is a separate movement.

preserved: Default behaviour for records without the flag remains exited_without_close
state_updates: Placed the handed_over rule after terminal and awaiting_po rules, exactly where HB-3 dictates.
